blogs.title: Hyponatremia, Headache, and Hiccups: Spotting SIADH from Neuroinflammation
blogs.description: A practical approach to hypotonic hyponatremia when CNS symptoms are present. Covers diagnosing SIADH (urine osmolality and sodium, exclusion of thyroid/adrenal disease), pitfalls of relying on volume exam alone, why hiccups and rhabdomyolysis can be clues to severe hyponatremia, and safe correction strategies (when to just restrict fluids vs use hypertonic saline or vaptans).

blogs.title: Neuro‑Behçet’s with a Normal MRI: Don’t Be Reassured by Clean Imaging
blogs.description: Clinical pearls for diagnosing acute neuro‑Behçet’s when MRI is unrevealing. Reviews the role of CSF (mild lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein), the timing of repeat imaging, how to balance empiric antivirals/antimicrobials while excluding infection, and why mucocutaneous cues should drive suspicion despite negative radiology.

blogs.title: When Behçet’s and Neuro‑Behçet’s Present Together: Building the Diagnosis at the Bedside
blogs.description: A bedside framework using the International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease. Highlights the diagnostic weight of genital ulcers, the limited utility of HLA‑B51, and the importance of serial exams as new lesions evolve. Discusses avoiding shotgun autoimmune/oncologic testing (ACE, sIL‑2R) without supportive clinical features.

blogs.title: Colchicine Alone for Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s? A Steroid‑Sparing Curveball
blogs.description: Examines the management controversy: corticosteroids are standard for neuro‑BD, yet this case improved on colchicine monotherapy. Reviews available evidence, potential for spontaneous resolution, patient selection when steroids are undesirable (e.g., diabetes), dosing and safety of colchicine, and clear triggers to escalate to steroids or immunosuppressants.

blogs.title: IL‑6, ADH, and the Inflamed Brain: Why SIADH Happens in Neuro‑BD
blogs.description: Translates pathophysiology into practice: how neuroinflammation and cytokines (especially IL‑6) can drive non‑osmotic ADH release. Summarizes the literature linking CSF IL‑6 elevations in neuro‑BD to SIADH, practical proxies like CRP, and why treating the underlying inflammation often corrects the sodium.

blogs.title: CK Through the Roof: Rhabdomyolysis as a Consequence of Severe Hyponatremia
blogs.description: Explores the under‑recognized link between profound hypotonicity and muscle injury. When to check CK in hyponatremic patients with malaise/arthralgia, how to balance fluid restriction in SIADH with the need to manage rhabdomyolysis, and strategies to avoid over‑correction and osmotic demyelination.

blogs.title: Hyponatremia in the Hyperglycemic Patient: Correct the Sodium, Not the Patient
blogs.description: A rapid bedside guide to differentiating true hypotonic hyponatremia from translocational or pseudohyponatremia. Provides correction formulas for hyperglycemia, ties osmolality to clinical decision‑making, and prevents mislabeling in diabetics presenting with CNS symptoms.

blogs.title: Headache, Fever, and a Rash: The High‑Yield Skin Exam that Changes Your Neuro Workup
blogs.description: Shows how targeted skin and mucosal findings (oral aphthae, folliculitis‑like lesions, later genital ulcers) can pivot the differential toward Behçet’s and away from infection or malignancy. Includes a stepwise ED/inpatient approach and timing for re‑examination when early features are incomplete.
